title: Korea Democracy Foundation Act
full_text:
KOREA DEMOCRACY FOUNDATION ACT

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to contribute to the development of democracy by establishing the Korea Democracy Foundation to carry out projects to commemorate the democratization movement and carry forward its spirit.

Article 2 (Definition)
The term “democratization movement” as used in this Act means activities prescribed by Presidential Decree that, since the establishment of the Government of the Republic of Korea on August 15, 1948, have restored and expanded the freedoms and rights of the people by resisting authoritarian rule that infringed upon their fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution, including the February 28 Daegu Democratization Movement, the March 8 Daejeon Democratic Uprising, the March 15 Uprising, the April 19 Revolution, the Busan-Masan Uprising, the May 3 Incheon Democratic Uprising, and the June 10 Uprising. <Amended on May 22, 2013; August 16, 2023>

Article 3 (Legal Personality)
The Korea Democracy Foundation (hereinafter referred to as the “Foundation”) shall be a corporation.

Article 4 (Establishment)
(1) The Foundation shall be established upon registration of its incorporation at the location of its principal office.
(2) The following matters shall be registered for incorporation under paragraph (1):
1. Purpose;
2. Name;
3. Location of the principal office;
4. Names and addresses of officers;
5. Method of giving public notice.

Article 5 (Articles of Incorporation)
(1) The articles of incorporation of the Foundation shall include the following matters:
1. Purpose;
2. Name;
3. Location of the principal office;
4. Matters concerning its projects and their implementation;
5. Matters concerning its organization;
6. Matters concerning officers and employees;
7. Matters concerning the operation of the board of directors;
8. Matters concerning assets and accounting;
9. Matters concerning amendments to the articles of incorporation;
10. Matters concerning the method of giving public notice.
(2) Where the Foundation intends to amend its articles of incorporation, it shall obtain authorization from the Minister of the Interior and Safety. <Amended on March 23, 2013; November 19, 2014; July 26, 2017>

Article 6 (Projects)
The Foundation shall carry out the following projects to achieve the purpose specified in Article 1:
1. Construction and operation of the Democratization Movement Memorial Hall (hereinafter referred to as the “Memorial Hall”);
2. Collection, preservation, digitization, management, exhibition, publicity, investigation, and research of historical materials to document the history of the democratization movement;
3. Preservation, management, investigation, publicity, and research of historic sites of the democratization movement;
4. Projects and events to commemorate and carry forward the democratization movement;
5. Support projects for democratic development;
6. Publicity for the Foundation and the Memorial Hall and production and distribution of various publications concerning them;
7. Profit-making projects for the operation of the Foundation;
8. Projects incidental to the projects specified in subparagraphs 1 through 7.

Article 7 (Officers)
(1) The Foundation shall have, as its officers, not more than 15 directors, including one chairperson and not more than five vice chairpersons, and two auditors.
(2) The chairperson shall be appointed and dismissed by the Minister of the Interior and Safety; vice chairpersons shall be selected by the board of directors; and directors shall be appointed and dismissed by the Minister of the Interior and Safety upon the recommendation of the chairperson. <Amended on March 23, 2013; November 19, 2014; July 26, 2017>
(3) Auditors shall be appointed and dismissed by the Minister of the Interior and Safety. <Amended on March 23, 2013; November 19, 2014; July 26, 2017>
(4) No more than three officers shall serve on a full-time basis, and the positions and number of full-time officers shall be prescribed by the articles of incorporation.

Article 8 (Terms of Office of Officers)
(1) The term of office of a director shall be three years and may be renewed. The terms of office of the chairperson and vice chairpersons shall be the same as those of directors.
(2) The term of office of an auditor shall be two years and may be renewed.

Article 9 (Duties of Officers)
(1) The chairperson shall represent the Foundation, exercise overall control over its affairs, and direct and supervise its employees.
(2) Where the chairperson is unable to perform his or her duties due to unavoidable circumstances, an officer shall act on the chairperson’s behalf as prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
(3) Directors shall attend meetings of the board of directors, deliberate and resolve upon important matters concerning the affairs of the Foundation, and handle matters delegated by the board of directors or the chairperson.
(4) Auditors shall audit matters concerning the affairs, operation, and accounting of the Foundation.

Article 10 (Disqualifications for Officers)
No person falling under any of the following subparagraphs may become an officer of the Foundation:
1. A person who is not a national of the Republic of Korea;
2. A person falling under any ground for disqualification specified in the subparagraphs of Article 33 of the State Public Officials Act;
3. A person prohibited by the articles of incorporation from becoming an officer.

Article 11 (Board of Directors)
(1) The Foundation shall have a board of directors to deliberate and resolve upon important matters concerning its affairs.
(2) The board of directors shall consist of the directors, including the chairperson and vice chairpersons.
(3) The chairperson shall convene meetings of the board of directors and preside over them: Provided, That where a request to convene a meeting of the board of directors is supported by at least one-third of the incumbent directors, the chairperson shall convene the meeting without delay.
(4) Unless otherwise specifically provided in the articles of incorporation, resolutions of the board of directors shall require the attendance of a majority of the incumbent directors and the affirmative vote of a majority of the directors present.
(5) Auditors may attend meetings of the board of directors and state their opinions.

Article 12 (Functions of the Board of Directors)
The board of directors shall deliberate and resolve upon the following matters:
1. Matters concerning project plans, budgets, and settlement of accounts;
2. Matters concerning amendments to the articles of incorporation;
3. Matters concerning dissolution of the Foundation;
4. Matters concerning the appointment and dismissal of officers;
5. Matters concerning the acquisition, management, and disposal of property;
6. Matters within its authority under the articles of incorporation;
7. Other matters important to the operation of the Foundation that the chairperson submits to a meeting.

Article 13 (Secretariat)
(1) The Foundation shall have a secretariat to handle its affairs.
(2) Matters concerning the secretariat shall be prescribed by the articles of incorporation.

Article 14 (Subsidies and Contributions)
(1) The State and local governments may subsidize expenses necessary for the Foundation to carry out its projects and affairs within budgetary limits.
(2) Any individual, corporation, or organization may contribute or donate money or other property to the Foundation to support the performance of its affairs.

Article 15 (Lending of State Property Free of Charge)
The State or a local government may, when necessary for the establishment and operation of the Foundation, lend State property or public property to the Foundation free of charge, notwithstanding the State Property Act or the Public Property and Commodity Management Act.

Article 16 (Admission Fees and Use Fees)
The Foundation may collect admission fees to the Memorial Hall and fees for the use of the materials or facilities of the Memorial Hall.

Article 17 (Fiscal Year)
The fiscal year of the Foundation shall coincide with the fiscal year of the Government.

Article 18 (Approval of Business Plans and Budgets)
(1) The Foundation shall submit a business plan and budget for each fiscal year to the Minister of the Interior and Safety for approval before the beginning of the relevant fiscal year. The same shall apply when it changes the major contents of an approved business plan and budget. <Amended 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>
(2) The business plan and budget referred to in paragraph (1) shall separately specify objectives, policies, the details of major projects, and the required budget, and shall be accompanied by materials necessary to clarify their contents. The same shall apply when they are amended.

Article 19 (Reporting on the Settlement of Accounts)
The Foundation shall prepare a statement of the settlement of revenue and expenditure for each fiscal year, have it examined by a certified public accountant, and submit it to the Minister of the Interior and Safety within 60 days after the end of the relevant fiscal year. <Amended 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>

Article 20 (Requests for the Provision of Materials)
(1) The Foundation may request the inspection, copying, lending, exhibition on consignment, etc. of materials from State agencies, local governments, educational institutions, research organizations, and other relevant persons.
(2) Any person who receives a request under paragraph (1) shall cooperate with such request unless there is a special reason not to do so.

Article 21 (Guidance and Supervision)
The Minister of the Interior and Safety shall guide and supervise the affairs of the Foundation. <Amended 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>

Article 22 (Application Mutatis Mutandis)
Except as otherwise provided in this Act, the provisions of the Act on the Establishment and Operation of Public Interest Corporations and the Civil Act concerning incorporated foundations shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Foundation.

ADDENDA <Act No. 6495, July 24, 2001>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force on the date on which three months have elapsed after its promulgation.

Article 2 (Preparations for Establishment)
(1) The Minister of Government Administration and Home Affairs shall commission not more than 10 establishment committee members of the Foundation before this Act enters into force to handle matters relating to its establishment.

(2) The establishment committee members shall prepare the articles of incorporation pursuant to Article 5 (1) within 30 days from the date they are commissioned and obtain authorization from the Minister of Government Administration and Home Affairs.

(3) The first chairperson of the Foundation shall be appointed by the Minister of Government Administration and Home Affairs.

(4) When the establishment committee members have obtained authorization for the articles of incorporation from the Minister of Government Administration and Home Affairs pursuant to paragraph (2), they shall, without delay, register the establishment of the Foundation pursuant to Article 3 in their joint names and then hand over their duties to the chairperson.

(5) The establishment committee members shall be deemed discharged from their appointments when they have handed over their duties pursuant to paragraph (4).

Article 3 (Special Provisions concerning Commencement Date of Terms of Office of Officers)
The terms of office of officers first appointed after this Act enters into force shall commence on the date of registration of the establishment of the Foundation.

Article 4 (Bearing of Expenses)
The State shall bear the expenses of establishing the Foundation.

Article 5 (Submission of Business Plans, etc.)
Notwithstanding Article 18, the business plan and budget for the fiscal year in which the enforcement date of this Act falls shall be submitted within two months from the date of registration of the establishment of the Foundation.
